description: Percent of amounts, discounts, profit and change

lessons.title: What is Percent?
lessons.intro: 'Percent' means 'out of 100'. When your test says 80%, it means 80 marks out of every 100!
explanation: The symbol % is short for 'per hundred'.
50% means 50 out of 100, which is half.
Percentages make it easy to compare different amounts fairly.
lessons.rule: Percent means 'out of 100'.
lessons.tip: Read % as 'out of a hundred'.

steps.text: Percent is a fraction with denominator 100.

lessons.title: Percent as a Fraction
lessons.intro: Any percentage can be written as a fraction over 100, then simplified.
explanation: Divide top and bottom by the same number to simplify.
lessons.rule: Percent to fraction: put it over 100 and simplify.
lessons.tip: Learn the friendly ones: 25%, 50%, 75%.

lessons.title: Percent as a Decimal
lessons.intro: To turn a percent into a decimal, divide by 100 — the point moves two places left.
explanation: Dividing by 100 shifts the decimal point two places left.
lessons.rule: Percent to decimal: divide by 100.
lessons.tip: Move the point two places to the left.

lessons.title: Common Percentages
lessons.intro: A few percentages come up again and again — knowing them by heart saves time.
explanation: 100% is the whole thing; 50% is half; 25% is a quarter.
10% is one tenth — just divide by 10.
1% is one hundredth.
lessons.tip: 10% of a number is simply that number / 10.

lessons.title: Why Percentages Help
lessons.intro: Percentages let us compare things of different sizes on the same fair scale.
explanation: Scoring 18/20 and 45/50 — percentages (90% each) show they are equal.
Shops use % for discounts so deals are easy to compare.
Percentages turn every amount into 'out of 100'.
lessons.rule: Percent puts everything on the same 'out of 100' scale.
lessons.tip: Convert to % to compare unlike amounts.

quiz.question: Write 25% as a fraction in lowest terms.
Write 50% as a decimal.
Write 7% as a decimal.
quiz.hint: Move the point two places left.

quiz.question: Write 75% as a fraction in lowest terms.
In a class, 50% of the students are girls. What fraction of the class is girls? Give it in lowest terms.
A phone battery is at 20%. Write this as a fraction in lowest terms.
quiz.story: Checking the battery before a trip.

quiz.question: Write 125% as a decimal.
Write 0.4 as a percentage. Include the % sign.

levels.label: Percent of a Number
levels.subtitle: Taking a part of an amount

lessons.title: Finding a Percent of a Number
lessons.intro: To find a percentage of an amount, turn the percent into a fraction (or decimal) and multiply.
explanation: Think: 'of' means 'multiply'.
50% of anything is just half of it.
lessons.rule: Percent of a number = (percent/100) x number.
lessons.tip: 'of' means multiply.

steps.text: Turn the percent into a fraction over 100.

lessons.title: Easy 10% Trick
lessons.intro: Finding 10% is super quick — just divide the number by 10.
explanation: Once you know 10%, you can build 20%, 30%, and more.
lessons.rule: 10% of a number = number / 10.
lessons.tip: Double 10% to get 20%.

lessons.title: Finding 25% and 50%
lessons.intro: 50% is half; 25% is a quarter. These are the friendliest percentages.
explanation: 25% is half of 50%.
lessons.rule: 50% = half; 25% = quarter.
lessons.tip: Halve twice to get a quarter.

lessons.title: Building Any Percentage
lessons.intro: Combine the easy pieces: 30% is three lots of 10%, 15% is 10% + 5%.
explanation: Break the percent into 10% and 5% chunks.
lessons.rule: Build tricky percents from 10% and 5% pieces.
lessons.tip: 5% is half of 10%.

lessons.title: Percent in Real Life
lessons.intro: Shops, exams and surveys use 'percent of' all the time.
explanation: A 20% tip on Rs 300 is Rs 60.
Scoring 80% on a 50-mark test is 40 marks.
Reading the question tells you the amount and the percent.
lessons.rule: Identify the amount, then take the percent of it.
lessons.tip: Underline the number and the percent first.

quiz.question: What is 10% of 50?
What is 50% of 60?
What is 25% of 80?
What is 20% of 150?
A shirt costs 400 rupees. A tailor's charge is 15% of this. What is the charge in rupees?
Out of 50 marks, Riya scored 80%. How many marks did she get?
What is 30% of 200?
What is 12% of 250?

lessons.title: Fractions to Percentages
lessons.intro: To turn a fraction into a percentage, make the denominator 100 (or multiply the fraction by 100).
lessons.rule: Fraction to percent: multiply by 100.
lessons.tip: Make the bottom 100, then read the top.

steps.text: Scale the fraction so the denominator is 100.
The numerator is now the percentage.

lessons.title: Decimals to Percentages
lessons.intro: To change a decimal into a percentage, multiply by 100 — the point moves two places right.
explanation: Multiplying by 100 shifts the point two places right.
lessons.rule: Decimal to percent: multiply by 100.
lessons.tip: Move the point two places right, add %.

lessons.title: Marks as Percentages
lessons.intro: Turning a test score into a percentage shows how you did out of 100.
explanation: Write the score as a fraction, then convert.
This lets you compare tests of different totals.
lessons.rule: Score percent = (marks / total) x 100.
lessons.tip: Divide marks by total, then x100.

lessons.title: One Amount as a Percent of Another
lessons.intro: We can say what fraction one amount is of another, as a percentage.
explanation: 15 is what percent of 60? 15/60 = 1/4 = 25%.
Make a fraction (part/whole) and convert.
The 'whole' is what comes after 'of'.
lessons.rule: Part as percent of whole = (part/whole) x 100.
lessons.tip: The whole goes on the bottom.

lessons.title: Percentages Compared
lessons.intro: Converting everything to percentages lets you compare fairly.
explanation: Always convert to the same scale first.
The bigger percentage is the better result (for scores).
lessons.rule: Convert each to % before comparing.
lessons.tip: Same scale makes comparison easy.

quiz.question: Write 1/2 as a percentage. Include the % sign.
Write 3/4 as a percentage. Include the % sign.
Write 0.6 as a percentage. Include the % sign.
Write 1/5 as a percentage. Include the % sign.
Aman scored 18 out of 20 in a test. What is his score as a percentage? Include the % sign.
In a box of 60 pens, 15 are red. What percentage are red? Include the % sign.
Write 0.125 as a percentage. Include the % sign.
27 is what percentage of 90? Include the % sign.

lessons.title: Discounts
lessons.intro: A discount is a percentage taken OFF the price. Find the discount, then subtract it.
explanation: A 20% discount on Rs 500 is Rs 100 off.
New price = 500 - 100 = Rs 400.
Discount reduces what you pay.
lessons.rule: Discount amount = percent x price; new price = price - discount.
lessons.tip: First find the discount, then subtract.

lessons.title: Sale Price Shortcut
lessons.intro: If 20% is taken off, you still PAY 80%. You can find the sale price in one step.
explanation: Pay 100% - 20% = 80% of the price.
This one-step trick saves time.
lessons.rule: Sale price = (100% - discount%) of the price.
lessons.tip: Subtract the discount percent from 100 first.

lessons.title: Increases
lessons.intro: Some things go UP by a percent — like a price rise. Find the increase, then add it.
explanation: A 10% rise on Rs 200 is Rs 20 more.
New price = 200 + 20 = Rs 220.
Increase makes the amount bigger.
lessons.rule: Increase amount = percent x amount; new = amount + increase.
lessons.tip: Find the rise, then add it on.

lessons.title: Money and Percentages
lessons.intro: Tips, taxes and savings are all percentages of money.
explanation: A 5% tax on Rs 400 is Rs 20.
A 10% tip on Rs 300 is Rs 30.
Add tax/tip; subtract discounts.
lessons.rule: Add for tax/tip, subtract for discount.
lessons.tip: Decide add or subtract before you start.

lessons.title: Mixed Money Problems
lessons.intro: Real shopping often mixes discounts and totals — take them one step at a time.
explanation: Rs 250 item with 20% off: pay Rs 200.
Buy 2 at the sale price: 2 x 200 = Rs 400.
Do the percentage first, then the counting.
lessons.rule: Handle the percentage step before multiplying quantities.
lessons.tip: Work in small, clear steps.

quiz.question: A 20% discount on 500 rupees is how many rupees off?
A 10% rise on 200 rupees adds how many rupees?
After a 20% discount, what is the sale price of a 500-rupee item, in rupees?
After a 10% rise, what is the new price of a 200-rupee item, in rupees?
A toy costs 250 rupees. In a sale it is 20% off. What is the sale price in rupees?
A meal costs 300 rupees. A 10% service tip is added. What is the total bill in rupees?
A 1200-rupee bag has 25% off. What is the sale price in rupees?
Two notebooks cost 250 rupees each with 20% off each. What is the total paid in rupees?
quiz.hint: Find one sale price, then double.

lessons.title: Finding the Whole
lessons.intro: Sometimes you know the percentage amount and must find the original whole.
explanation: If 10% of a number is 7, the number is 70.
Work backwards: whole = part / (percent/100).
This 'reverse percentage' is a powerful skill.
lessons.rule: Whole = part / (percent as a fraction).
lessons.tip: If 10% is known, multiply it by 10 for the whole.

steps.text: 10% is one tenth of the whole.
So the whole is ten times the part.

lessons.title: Percentage Change
lessons.intro: Percentage change tells us how much something grew or shrank, as a percent of the start.
explanation: A price goes 100 -> 120: that is a 20% increase.
Change% = (change / original) x 100.
The original amount is always the base.
lessons.rule: Change% = (new - old)/old x 100.
lessons.tip: Always divide the change by the ORIGINAL.

lessons.title: Combining Percentages
lessons.intro: Careful! 10% then another 10% is not 20% of the start, because the base changes.
explanation: Each percentage applies to the newest amount.
Do the steps one after another.
lessons.rule: Apply each percentage to the current amount in turn.
lessons.tip: Never just add the percents together.

lessons.title: Profit and Percentages
lessons.intro: Shopkeepers describe profit as a percentage of the cost price.
explanation: Buy at Rs 200, sell at Rs 250: profit Rs 50.
The cost price is the base for profit%.
lessons.rule: Profit% = (profit / cost) x 100.
lessons.tip: Cost price goes on the bottom.

lessons.title: Percentage Master
lessons.intro: Put it all together: of, change, discount and reverse percentages.
explanation: Read carefully to spot the base amount.
Decide: are you finding a part, a whole, or a change?
Check your answer is a sensible size.
lessons.rule: Identify part, whole, or change — then choose the method.
lessons.tip: A quick estimate catches silly errors.

quiz.question: If 10% of a number is 7, what is the number?
A price rises from 100 to 120 rupees. What is the percentage increase? Include the % sign.
If 25% of a number is 15, what is the number?
quiz.hint: 25% is a quarter, so multiply by 4.

quiz.question: An item bought for 200 rupees is sold for 250 rupees. What is the profit percentage? Include the % sign.
20% of the students in a school play cricket. If 40 students play cricket, how many students are there in all?
quiz.hint: 40 is 20%, so the whole is 5 times 40.

quiz.question: A shopkeeper buys a toy for 150 rupees and sells it for 180 rupees. What is the profit percentage? Include the % sign.
Rs 100 is increased by 10%, then the result is increased by 10% again. What is the final amount in rupees?
If 15% of a number is 45, what is the number?
